detailed_findings.finding: Argument is mathematically complete under the stated convention that N starts at 1, ensuring the real power (g(g(n)))^r is well-defined even for negative r.

reason: The proof correctly computes g(n+1)-g(n)=2n+1 and g(g(n))=n^4, then shows (g(g(n)))^r=n^{4r} for positive n. Using r<=1/4 and n>=1, it derives n^{4r}<=n<=2n+1, which proves the desired inequality for all n in the stated domain. This matches the lemma sketch and supports the root theorem's witness construction.
